label: D1 after a rewarded common trial when the agent is about to choose a1
explanation: Fires only at D1 (never at GO or D2). About 95% of activation mass falls where the reward input is 1 (the previous trial was rewarded) and the agent goes on to choose a1 (its own upcoming choice; the D1 policy logit is positive, 92% of mass in choice 2.8-8). It is almost silent after rare transitions (prev_common=0: 0.1% rate), so it marks a rewarded common trial (or the window start, where prev_common is unknown) that supports the a1/S1 option. That is the model-based stay-on-a1 signal. Does not fire on unrewarded D1s (prev_reward=0: about 5% of mass, weak) or when the agent heads for a2. Dev scores: phase&action==1 alone gives F1 0.73, adding prev_reward==1 gives 0.84, and excluding prev rare gives 0.88. The leftover misses are weak activations at unrewarded D1s that precede an a1 choice. Uses only observed inputs plus the agent own upcoming choice. Magnitude is not characterised beyond this: low-quartile activations are less well covered (72%) than the top quartile (99.6%).

issues: The factual claims hold on the test split. The feature fires only at D1: (phase != D1) gives F1 0. It is silent after rare transitions: D1 & action==1 & prev_common==0 has precision 0.008. The ladder D1&action==1 (0.715) -> +prev_reward==1 (0.827) -> +prev_common!=0 (0.872) matches what was reported.

The label leaves out that the previous choice was a1, which the predicate implies. After a2-common-rewarded with an a1 choice there are only 36 steps, all inactive (precision 0). Using prev_action==1 & prev_common==1 & prev_reward==1, or the window start with action==1, gives the same F1 0.871. So the predicate amounts to 'a1 -> S1 was rewarded and the agent stays on a1'. A better label would be 'D1 after a1 led to S1 and was rewarded (stay on a1)'.

There is one small systematic class of misses. When the previous trial was a1, common and unrewarded and the agent stays on a1, the feature fires 50% of the time. That is 8.5% of active steps but only 4% of mass, and the activations are weak. It fits the explanation's note about weak unrewarded D1s that come before an a1 choice.

The false positives (about 15% of predicted steps) are spread evenly. Precision is about 0.85 for good=S1, good=S2, prev_common=1 and the window start alike, so they look like a threshold effect rather than a hidden condition. Adding the D1 policy logit (choice > 1.5) raises precision to 0.90 (F1 0.896).
Adding a gated choice-logit term gives test F1 0.904, mass recall 0.99. That is a modest gain from a model-internal variable, not a refutation.
skeptic.revised_label: D1 after the agent's a1 choice reached S1 (common) and was rewarded, as it stays on a1 (weakly after a common unrewarded a1 trial)
